## EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

**What changes:** Moving Motivators stops being a field the facilitator fills in manually inside the authenticated form. Instead, the facilitator shares one **generic public URL** with the architect. The architect — with no account — self-reports through a two-step Management 3.0–style exercise (horizontal card ranking, then up/center/down impact placement). The result is stored server-side and surfaces **read-only** in the facilitator's authenticated view (Preparar phase) and in aggregate on the Home dashboard, replacing the current single motivator radar with **two charts** (radar + priority bar), averaged **per macrodomain (team)**.

**Core tension this addendum resolves:** the public form has no `auth.uid()`, but every existing table is scoped by Supabase RLS to a logged-in facilitator's `user_id`. The resolution (detailed in Ambiguity #1) is to **not** write public submissions into the existing RLS-protected tables at all. They land in a new, independent table keyed by **email**, and the authenticated side reads from it via a **matching join at display time** — never a write-time ownership guess.

---

## AMBIGUITY RESOLUTION

| # | Ambiguity | Decision | Rationale |
|---|-----------|----------|-----------|
| 1 | **Ownership under RLS.** A public, unauthenticated submitter cannot write into `gemba_records`/`gemba_moving_motivators`, which are scoped to `auth.uid()`. Who is the "owner"? | **Don't assign an owner at write time.** Create a new table `moving_motivator_submissions`, written only via a backend service-role endpoint, **not** linked to any `user_id`. At **read time**, the facilitator's authenticated backend call joins the architect's `gemba_records` row to a submission by matching `architect_email`. No RLS rewrite needed, no guessing which facilitator "owns" an architect who has no account. |
| 2 | **Identity matching** — same name in different macrodomains, or matching to an existing record. **[Updated per user clarification, 2026-11-17]** | Match a new submission against existing `moving_motivator_submissions` rows by **name OR email** (case-insensitive, trimmed) — not email alone. The facilitator-side join (`gemba_records.architect_email` ↔ submission `email`) is unaffected by this and still uses email only, since that join is about linking a known record to its result, not detecting duplicates among incoming public submissions. |
| 3 | **Resubmission / duplicates** — same architect fills the form twice, or a name/email collision is detected. **[Updated per user clarification, 2026-11-17]** | **Delete-and-replace, with explicit confirmation — never silent, never blocked.** No `UNIQUE` DB constraint drives this (removed); the backend actively checks name/email overlap on every submission. If a duplicate is found, the user is **not** auto-overwritten and is **not** rejected — they see a confirmation step ("Ya existe un registro con este nombre o correo de %fecha%. Si continúas, se eliminará el anterior y se guardará esta nueva información.") and must explicitly confirm before the old row is deleted and the new one inserted. See full UX flow in **#10** below. Rationale: silent overwrite risks destroying a different real person's data on a name-only collision; a hard block frustrates legitimate resubmission (e.g., architect corrects a mistake); confirm-before-delete is the one extra click that makes a destructive action safe without being a nuisance. |
| 4 | **Abuse / spam** on a tokenless, login-free URL. | **In-scope minimal guardrails, no CAPTCHA.** IP-based rate limiting (5 submissions/hour/IP via `@nestjs/throttler`), strict email format + required-field validation, macrodomain must come from a controlled list (see §3.2). CAPTCHA / per-architect tokens are **explicitly out of scope for this MVP** — documented as a future hardening step if abuse is observed in the pilot (hypothesis-1 scope is a handful of architects, not public internet traffic). |
| 5 | **Impact range migration** (old `-1..1`-ish slider vs. new `-4..+4`). | **No migration — clean cutover.** The old `gemba_moving_motivators` table is **frozen** (kept in DB for historical export/print of existing records, no longer written to). The new table defines `impact INT CHECK (impact BETWEEN -4 AND 4)` from scratch. No column type change, no backfill — avoids corrupting historical data with a lossy rescale. |
| 6 | **Preparar UI**: pedido says "only shows the result" (read-only). Keep manual edit as fallback? | **Remove `MotivatorList.tsx` editing entirely from the authenticated form.** Preparar now shows either: (a) read-only radar + bar if a matching submission exists, or (b) a "pending architect self-assessment" empty state with a **copy-link button** for the public URL. No manual-edit fallback — the whole point of this addendum is that only the architect's own hand should set these values; a facilitator-editable fallback would silently reintroduce proxy-reporting, which undermines the Management 3.0 exercise's validity. |
| 7 | **Bar chart orientation** — "most relevant stuck to the Y axis, successively to the right." | **Vertical column chart.** X-axis = motivators ordered left→right by ascending average `priorityOrder` (1 = most important). Y-axis = priority score, scaled `10 − priorityOrder` so the tallest bar is the most important motivator, sitting immediately next to the Y-axis on the left. This matches the literal instruction and keeps the existing `BarChart.tsx` component (already renders vertical bars for gap classification) reusable without a new orientation variant. |
| 8 | **Team average formula** (per macrodomain, radar + bars). | **Radar:** arithmetic mean of `impact` (−4..4) per motivator across all submissions whose `macrodomain` matches the filter, clamped to range. **Bars:** arithmetic mean of `priorityOrder` (1..10) per motivator across the same filtered set, then sort ascending by that mean (lowest avg = most important = leftmost bar). Both recompute live from `moving_motivator_submissions` filtered by macrodomain — no caching/materialization needed at pilot scale (≤500 architects per original spec's scope slider). |
| 9 | **Macrodomain source in public form.** **[User-confirmed, 2026-11-17, final spelling confirmed 2026-11-17 — supersedes my original "dynamic list + 'Otro' fallback" proposal]** | **Fixed, closed list of exactly 5 values, in this order, no free text, no "Otro":** `CX & Engagement`, `Business Line`, `Enterprise Technology`, `Enablement Service`, `Technology Foundation`. Hardcoded as a shared constant (`PUBLIC_MACRODOMAINS`) used both in the frontend `<select>` and as a server-side whitelist on submit (reject anything not in the list). The `GET /api/public/macrodomains` endpoint originally proposed is **removed** — it's no longer needed since the list is static, not derived from existing data. This exact string set is also the matching key for Home's per-macrodomain filter, so it must byte-match wherever `gemba_records.macrodomain` is filtered against it. |
| 10 | **Duplicate-confirmation UX flow — exact mechanics.** **[My decision, per user's "usa tu criterio" instruction, 2026-11-17]** | Single endpoint, two-pass: (1) architect clicks "Enviar" → `POST /api/public/moving-motivators` with no override flag → backend checks name/email overlap → if found, responds `409` with the existing record's name/email/`submittedAt`, **nothing is written yet**; frontend shows a confirmation modal ("Ya existe un registro con este nombre o correo, de [fecha]. Si continúas, se eliminará el anterior y se guardará esta nueva información.") with **Reemplazar** / **Cancelar**. (2) If the architect clicks **Reemplazar**, frontend resubmits the identical payload with `confirmReplace: true` → backend deletes the matched row(s) and inserts the new one fresh, returns `201`. If **Cancelar**, nothing happens — architect can edit Step 0 and retry with different info. No duplicate check blocks the happy path (first-time submitters see no modal, straight to confirmation screen). |

## FEATURE SPECIFICATION

### 1. Overview

Two independent surfaces:

1. **Public wizard** (no login) — `/motivadores` — 3 screens: Identificación → Paso 1 (ordenar) → Paso 2 (impacto) → confirmación.
2. **Authenticated surfaces** (existing facilitator login) — Preparar tab (per-architect read-only result) + Home dashboard (team-averaged result, two charts replacing the current single motivator radar).

```
Public (no auth)                         Authenticated (existing facilitator)
─────────────────                        ─────────────────────────────────────
/motivadores                             Home
 ├─ Step 0: name/email/macrodomain        ├─ Radar de impacto (team avg)  ←NEW
 ├─ Step 1: drag-order 10 cards            ├─ Barras de prioridad (team avg) ←NEW
 ├─ Step 2: up/center/down (-4..+4)        └─ subtítulo: URL pública + copiar
 └─ Submit → thank-you screen
         │                                FormView → Preparar tab
         │  POST (service role,            ├─ (if match found) Radar + Barras
         │   confirm-then-replace          │   del arquitecto, read-only
         │   on name/email match)          └─ (if no match) "Pendiente de
         ▼                                     autoevaluación" + copy-link
 moving_motivator_submissions                       ▲
         └──────── matched by architect_email ──────┘
                    at read time (no write-time link)
```

### 2. Public Wizard (`/motivadores`)

**Route:** `/motivadores` — single generic URL, no token, no auth guard, publicly indexable-safe (no PII rendered, no architect data pre-filled).

**Step 0 — Identificación**
- Fields: `name` (text, required), `email` (email, required, validated format), `macrodomain` (select, required)
- Macrodomain is a **fixed, closed dropdown of exactly 5 values**, no free text (see Ambiguity #9):
  1. CX & Engagement
  2. Business Line
  3. Enterprise Technology
  4. Enablement Service
  5. Technology Foundation
  - This list is a shared constant (`PUBLIC_MACRODOMAINS`), also enforced server-side as a whitelist on submit — no "Otro" option, no dynamic fetch.
- "Siguiente" button disabled until all 3 fields valid.

**Step 1 — Ordenar (Management 3.0, Paso 1)**
- Renders the same 10 motivator cards as today's `MOT` constant (name + description), using the **official Management 3.0 card visuals/copy** already present in the prototype — no new content to author.
- Interaction: **horizontal drag-and-drop**, left→right. Convention (matches the official Moving Motivators exercise): **leftmost = least important, rightmost = most important.**
- Internally stored as `priorityOrder` 1..10 where **1 = most important** (i.e., rightmost card at submit time), decoupled from the visual drag direction — this is what the backend/bar-chart consume (see Ambiguity #7/#8).
- "Siguiente" enabled once all 10 cards have been placed (initial order is a neutral shuffle or the fixed `MOT` order — not pre-ranked, to avoid anchoring bias).

**Step 2 — Impacto (Management 3.0, Paso 2)**
- Same 10 cards, now arranged in a **vertical lane per card** (or a single shared vertical axis with 10 slots side by side — implementation detail left to the frontend engineer, functionally: one vertical position per card).
- Three zones: **Arriba** (favors, positive), **Centro** (neutral, 0), **Abajo** (does not favor, negative).
- Each zone maps to a draggable position on a **−4..+4** scale (not just 3 discrete buckets) — "up" and "down" are directions, but the exact magnitude within up/down is adjustable (matches pedido: "puede poner parametros arriba y abajo... el maximo es 4 y el minimo es -4").
- "Enviar" button → `POST /api/public/moving-motivators`.

**Confirmation screen**
- Simple "Gracias, tu información fue enviada" message. **No results shown to the architect** — results are only visible to the facilitator (this is a facilitator-observation tool, not a self-serve personality report).

### 3. Data Model

#### 3.1 New table: `moving_motivator_submissions`

```sql
CREATE TABLE public.moving_motivator_submissions (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  email VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  macrodomain VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL
    CHECK (macrodomain IN ('CX & Engagement','Business Line','Enterprise Technology','Enablement Service','Technology Foundation')),
  priorities JSONB NOT NULL,
    -- [{ "motivator": "Curiosidad", "priorityOrder": 3 }, ...]  (1 = most important, 10 = least)
  impacts JSONB NOT NULL,
    -- [{ "motivator": "Curiosidad", "impact": 2 }, ...]          (-4..+4)
  submitted_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  CONSTRAINT valid_priorities_count CHECK (jsonb_array_length(priorities) = 10),
  CONSTRAINT valid_impacts_count CHECK (jsonb_array_length(impacts) = 10)
);
-- NOTE: no UNIQUE(email) constraint — per Ambiguity #3/#10, duplicate detection
-- (by name OR email, case-insensitive) is handled in application logic with an
-- explicit confirm-before-delete step, not a DB-level upsert.
CREATE INDEX idx_mms_email_lower ON moving_motivator_submissions (lower(trim(email)));
CREATE INDEX idx_mms_name_lower ON moving_motivator_submissions (lower(trim(name)));

ALTER TABLE moving_motivator_submissions ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
-- No SELECT/INSERT/DELETE policy for `anon` or `authenticated` roles.
-- All access goes through the NestJS backend using the Supabase service-role key:
--   - INSERT/DELETE: public endpoint, service role, per the confirm-replace flow (#10)
--   - SELECT: authenticated endpoints only, service role, filtered server-side
```

#### 3.2 Schema change to existing table: `gemba_records`

```sql
ALTER TABLE public.gemba_records
  ADD COLUMN architect_email VARCHAR(255);
-- Nullable: existing records predate this field; facilitator backfills when editing.
-- Used ONLY as the join key to moving_motivator_submissions. Not unique (a facilitator
-- could theoretically mistype), validated as email format at the form layer.
```

#### 3.3 Deprecated (frozen, not dropped): `gemba_moving_motivators`

- No new INSERT/UPDATE from the application after this addendum ships.
- Existing rows remain for historical export/print of already-observed records.
- `MotivatorList.tsx` (drag + slider editor) is **removed** from the Preparar phase's render tree.

### 4. API Contract

```
# PUBLIC (no auth, rate-limited)
# No GET endpoint for macrodomains — PUBLIC_MACRODOMAINS is a fixed constant
# shared between frontend and backend (see Ambiguity #9).

POST /api/public/moving-motivators
  Body: {
    name: string,
    email: string,            // validated format
    macrodomain: string,      // must be one of the 5 PUBLIC_MACRODOMAINS values (exact match)
    priorities: [{ motivator: string, priorityOrder: 1..10 }],  // all 10, no duplicates
    impacts: [{ motivator: string, impact: -4..4 }],             // all 10, no duplicates
    confirmReplace?: boolean  // default false — see duplicate flow below (#10)
  }
  Response (first pass, no duplicate found): 201 { submittedAt: string }
  Response (first pass, duplicate found, confirmReplace=false):
    409 { duplicate: true, existing: { name, email, submittedAt } }
    // Nothing written yet. Frontend shows confirm modal, resubmits with confirmReplace:true.
  Response (confirmReplace=true): 201 { submittedAt: string }
    // Backend deletes matched row(s) by name OR email (case-insensitive), inserts fresh.
  Errors: 400 (validation — includes macrodomain not in whitelist), 429 (rate limit exceeded)
  Rate limit: 5 req/hour/IP (both passes count toward the same bucket)


# AUTHENTICATED (existing SupabaseAuthGuard, owner-scoped)

GET /api/records/:id/motivator-result
  Response: 200 {
    found: boolean,
    result?: {
      name, email, macrodomain, submittedAt,
      priorities: [{ motivator, priorityOrder }],
      impacts: [{ motivator, impact }]
    }
  }
  Logic: looks up gemba_records.architect_email for :id, joins
         moving_motivator_submissions by email. found=false if no
         architect_email set on the record, or no matching submission.
  Auth: owner only (existing guard pattern)

GET /api/dashboard/motivators-summary
  Query: ?macrodomain=X (optional; omitted = all)
  Response: 200 {
    sampleSize: number,                 // # of submissions included
    radar: [{ motivator, avgImpact }],        // 10 items, -4..4
    bars: [{ motivator, avgPriorityOrder }]   // 10 items, sorted ascending by avgPriorityOrder
  }
  Auth: required (any authenticated facilitator — team-level aggregate, no PII beyond
        motivator names/scores)
```

### 5. Frontend Changes

| Surface | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| **Preparar tab** | `MotivatorList.tsx`: 10 draggable cards + impact slider, editable, auto-saves to `gemba_moving_motivators` | `MotivatorResultView.tsx` (new, read-only): if `motivator-result.found` → `RadarChart` (impacts) + `BarChart` (priorities, sorted); else → empty state with "Pendiente de autoevaluación" + "Copiar enlace" button (copies the public `/motivadores` URL) |
| **Home dashboard** | Single `RadarChart` card: "Radar de motivadores" | Two cards: "Radar de impacto de motivadores" (`RadarChart`, team avg impacts) + "Prioridad de motivadores" (`BarChart`, team avg priority, vertical, most-important leftmost). Card/quadrant subtitle: the public URL + "Copiar" button. Both respect the existing macrodomain filter — refetch `motivators-summary?macrodomain=X` on filter change. |
| **New public route** | — | `/motivadores`: 3-screen wizard, no header/nav chrome from the authenticated app (standalone public layout) |

### 6. Reused Components (no changes needed)

- `RadarChart.tsx` — already generic (labels + values + color); consumed with new data shape.
- `BarChart.tsx` — already renders vertical bars (used today for gaps-by-type); consumed with motivator labels/values instead.

## IMPLEMENTATION PLAN

Each phase below is intentionally short and independently testable — no phase bundles frontend + backend + a new table at once.

### Phase A — Schema & Migration
**Scope:** Create `moving_motivator_submissions` table + RLS (no policies, service-role-only access). Add `architect_email` column to `gemba_records`. No application code.

**Deliverable:** Migration applied to Supabase; verifiable via SQL console that table/column exist with correct constraints.

### Phase B — Public Submission Endpoint
**Scope:** `POST /api/public/moving-motivators` — macrodomain whitelist validation, name/email duplicate check (case-insensitive), 409-then-confirm flow (`confirmReplace`), delete-and-replace logic, rate limiting. No frontend yet — test via HTTP client.

**Deliverable:** Endpoint live; first-submission path (201), duplicate-detected path (409 + no write), confirmed-replace path (delete old + insert new, 201) all verified.

### Phase C — Public Wizard: Step 0 (Identificación)
**Scope:** `/motivadores` route, Step 0 form only (name/email/macrodomain), client-side validation, macrodomain dropdown rendering the fixed 5-value `PUBLIC_MACRODOMAINS` constant (no API call, no free text). "Siguiente" navigates to an empty Step 1 placeholder.

**Deliverable:** Step 0 renders with the 5 fixed options in the specified order, validates, advances.

### Phase D — Public Wizard: Step 1 (Ordenar)
**Scope:** 10 Management-3.0-style cards, horizontal drag-and-drop reorder. Internal state tracks `priorityOrder` (1 = rightmost/most important). No backend call yet.

**Deliverable:** Drag-order works, order is internally consistent with the 1=most-important convention.

### Phase E — Public Wizard: Step 2 (Impacto) + Submit
**Scope:** Up/center/down placement per card on a −4..+4 scale, "Enviar" wired to `POST /api/public/moving-motivators`, confirmation screen, **and the duplicate-confirm modal** (409 response → modal with existing record's date → "Reemplazar" resubmits with `confirmReplace: true`, "Cancelar" returns to the wizard without submitting).

**Deliverable:** Full public flow works end-to-end for both first-time and duplicate submitters; a real submission lands in `moving_motivator_submissions`; a confirmed replace correctly removes the old row.

### Phase F — Authenticated Read Endpoints
**Scope:** `GET /api/records/:id/motivator-result` (email-matched join) + `GET /api/dashboard/motivators-summary` (macrodomain-filtered averages). No frontend yet — test via authenticated HTTP client.

**Deliverable:** Both endpoints return correct shapes against seeded submissions.

### Phase G — Preparar Tab: Read-Only Result
**Scope:** Remove `MotivatorList.tsx` from Preparar render tree. Add `MotivatorResultView.tsx` (found → charts; not found → pending state + copy-link). Requires facilitator to have entered `architect_email` in metadata (add the field to the metadata grid if not already exposed).

**Deliverable:** Preparar tab shows live result or pending state correctly for a given record.

### Phase H — Home Dashboard: Dual Charts + URL Subtitle
**Scope:** Replace single motivator radar card with two cards (radar + bar) sourced from `motivators-summary`, filter-aware (macrodomain). Add URL + "Copiar" subtitle to that quadrant.

**Deliverable:** Home shows both charts, both react to the macrodomain filter, URL copies correctly.

### Phase I — End-to-End Round Trip & Visual Regression
**Scope:** Full flow test: public submission → facilitator sees it in Preparar → Home aggregate updates. Playwright visual check against the design conventions already established in the base spec (colors, spacing, responsive breakpoints) applied to the new public wizard and new Home cards.

**Deliverable:** Round trip verified; new public wizard passes the same responsive/visual bar as the rest of the app.
